content.content:
## Pitch

The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

## Description

A ribbon runs along the top of the window, in the colours of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope), a row of tabs, 32 pixels tall, above the command area. The tabs are flat: each is only its label, with 8 pixels either side of it, and no borders, no rounded corners, and no line anywhere, neither between the tabs nor between the tab row and the commands. The tab row has a background of its own, a step lighter than the command area, #333333 in dark mode; a closed tab has no background
A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says more. Its tabs are, in order: Project, Code, Spec, and Application. The window always opens on Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups. There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

## Keyboard

<Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+4> opening Application. Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no tooltip.

## Opening Several Tabs

Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open. Every open tab shows as selected.
The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side, in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with the same divider between one tab's groups and the next as between any groups. An open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the same height however many tabs are open.
Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between

### Launches

the window always opens with only Project open.

## Left Container

At the left end of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach it, sits the left container. It holds, in order, the project indicator, the collapse chevron, and the activity spinner, and can hold other things after them. It is the same whether the ribbon is expanded, beside the tabs, or collapsed, leading the row of primary commands.
It runs from the top of the bar down to the line along its bottom, never over it, so it is the same height expanded and collapsed. Everything in it is vertically centred in that height, with no gap between one thing and the next and no padding around them: each thing's own size is all the room it takes. The container shrinks to fit what it holds, and when it holds nothing, it isn't there at all.

## Right Container

    description:
        The Code tab of the ribbon.

    colour:
        While closed, the tab's label is in Code's colour, at full strength,

        so the tab keeps the size and place it has closed, and its label never
        moves. Open beside other tabs, the tab is tinted and the command area,
        shared with them, is not.

    groups:
        A "Run" group holds the commands for running the project, as the
        @{RunTargetsScope} says: Find How to Run until the project has run
        targets, and then a button for each target, then Find Again.
